info.description: Hexagonal blog platform REST API. Envelope responses use { ok, code, data, meta, error }.
info.title: Blog API

post.description: Queues a ZIP of CSV files with every rollup (site, pages, referrers, audience, navigation, searches, search positions, clicked results) of whole periods covering from through to, plus the daily retention cohorts. No raw events, visitor hashes, or session ids are exported. Requires the current password, and two_factor_code when two-factor is enabled. The archive is built in the background: poll GET /api/v1/admin/analytics/exports/{param1} for a presigned download link. One export per user may be open; a second request answers 409 with the open one in error.details.

get.description: The caller's 20 most recent exports, newest first. Completed exports whose archive still exists carry a fresh presigned download_url valid for ANALYTICS_EXPORT_URL_TTL (never past archive_expires_at).

Status of one of the caller's exports; other users' exports answer 404. A completed export whose archive still exists carries a fresh presigned download_url; after ANALYTICS_EXPORT_RETENTION the archive is deleted and status is expired.
The most common steps between pages (with their transition type) and the top entry and exit pages.

Totals, a series per period, the top 10 traffic sources, and audience (country, device, browser) for whole periods of the site time zone. Visitors are distinct within a period; a range total is the sum of per-period uniques, named visitor_days, visitor_weeks, or visitor_months after the grain, and plain visitors appears only when the window is a single period. previous holds the same number of periods just before the window (null with compare=none). Rates are null when their denominator is zero.

parameters.description: first day, YYYY-MM-DD (default 29 days before to)
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: period length (default by range: up to 92 days day, up to 366 week, else month); day covers at most 92 days
parameters.name: grain

get.description: Top pages by views, average focus time (sort=time), or views gained over the previous window (sort=rising). previous_views and change appear with compare=previous or sort=rising. Pages outside the top 1000 of a period are folded into (other), which only sort=views lists.

Server-sent events. The stream opens with `retry: 5000` and `event: stream.opened`, then every 5 seconds (and once right away) sends `event: realtime.page_view` and `event: realtime.search` for events accepted since the previous frame (at most 20 of each, the latest when busier; the first frame replays up to 20 recent ones), followed by `event: realtime.summary`: sessions active in the last 5 minutes, views and searches per minute for the last 30 minutes, and the top 10 pages of those 30 minutes. The summary doubles as the heartbeat. `event: stream.closed` (code shutdown) precedes a server shutdown. Counts cover every API replica through the message broker but start empty when a replica starts. Page views carry path, country, and device; searches the normalised query and result count; nothing identifies a visitor. Returns 429 analytics.realtime_limit (with Retry-After) past the per-user stream limit and 503 analytics.realtime_unavailable without a message broker.

Daily cohorts of consented visitors first seen on each day of the window, with how many returned on day 1, 7, and 30 (null until that day has passed), weighted return rates over complete cohorts, and the new versus returning split of consented visitors.
Search totals and series, click-through rate, average seconds to the first click, top and zero-result queries, clicks per result position, and the most clicked results. Needs analytics.search.read.

post.description:
Same request, responses, lockout and two-factor challenge as POST /api/v1/auth/login,
but only accounts holding the `admin.access` permission may sign in. Any other
account gets the same 401 as a wrong password.

429.description: rate limited or account locked; see Retry-After

503.description: two-factor account but 2FA is not configured

get.description: Comments in any status across posts. Defaults to the moderation queue (pending and flagged), oldest first.

parameters.description: comma-separated statuses: pending, approved, flagged, spam, rejected, deleted
parameters.name: status

post.description: Applies one action to up to 500 comments in a single transaction: all change or none do. Unknown ids return 404 and disallowed transitions 409, both listing the offending ids in error.details.ids.

get.description: Any status, with author identity, flags, and the moderation log with before/after snapshots.

delete.description: Removes the comment row. A comment with replies is scrubbed instead (content and author erased, kept as a deleted placeholder) so its replies survive; outcome reports which happened. The action is recorded in the moderation log.

post.description: approve, reject, or spam a comment, or restore a deleted one. Returns 409 when the action is not allowed from the current status.

get.description:
Returns the session behind the impersonation token in the Authorization header, or the
caller's active session when called with their own token. data.session is null when there
is none.

post.description:
Opens an impersonation session and returns a Bearer token that acts as the target until
expires_at (IMPERSONATION_TTL, never renewed; no refresh token). Requires impersonation.start,
the caller's current password, and a TOTP or backup code when the caller has two-factor
enabled. The target must be active, must not be an administrator or able to impersonate, and
every permission the target has must be one the caller has. One active session per caller.
The session ends with the caller's own sign-in (logout, revocation, or refresh-session expiry).

Ends the session behind the impersonation token in the Authorization header, or the caller's
active session when called with their own token. The impersonation token stops working
immediately; the client switches back to the staff member's own token.

parameters.description: only ready assets no avatar, category, post cover, attachment, or SEO image references
parameters.name: unused

get.description: Counts and bytes of stored media by status (soft-deleted assets as deleted until the orphan cleanup purges them), content type, and top uploaders. user_id narrows the report to one uploader.

parameters.description: draft, scheduled, queued, sending, sent, cancelled
parameters.name: status

post.description:
status draft (default) saves; scheduled sends at send_at; queued sends now. Scheduling and
sending need newsletter.issues.send and a postal_address in the provider config. The Markdown
body is rendered to sanitized HTML and plain text inside a template that adds the unsubscribe
and preferences links and the postal address.
post.summary: Create, schedule, or send a newsletter issue

get.description: preview=true adds the rendered html and text as a subscriber would receive them.

patch.description:
Content and lists change only while draft or scheduled. status moves draft/scheduled to
draft, scheduled, queued, or cancelled; queued to cancelled; sending to queued (resume) or
cancelled. Scheduling and sending need newsletter.issues.send. 409 when the move is not
allowed or the issue changed meanwhile.
patch.summary: Update, schedule, send, or cancel a newsletter issue

get.description:
Stored sending settings and lists, and the read-only provider from the environment
(NEWSLETTER_PROVIDER); the HMAC secret is never returned, only whether it is set.

put.description:
Saves the sending settings and the complete list set. Lists missing from lists are archived:
they keep memberships and history but can no longer be joined or targeted. At least one list
must be a default list. The provider, endpoint, and secret are environment settings.

get.description:
Filters by status, list slug, and email prefix (q). format=csv downloads every matching
subscriber (up to 50000) as CSV and needs newsletter.subscribers.export.

parameters.description: pending_confirm, active, unsubscribed, bounced, complained, erased
parameters.name: status

get.description: The subscriber, list memberships, and the latest 100 consent events.

delete.summary: Unsubscribe or erase a newsletter subscriber

delete.description: Soft delete: the post leaves public and admin reads and releases its slug. List with trashed=true and restore to undo.

post.description: Hides a draft, scheduled, or published post from public reads; published_at is kept. Publish again to bring it back.
Allowed from draft, scheduled, or archived; sets published_at to now. Returns 409 post.invalid_transition for a post that is already published.
Brings a soft-deleted post back as a draft. If a live post took its slug meanwhile, the slug gets the lowest free numeric suffix (-2, -3, …).

get.description: Newest first. Authors see only their own posts' history; editors and admins (post.revisions.view_all) see every post's.

parameters.description: only revisions by this user UUID
parameters.name: author_id

parameters.description: RFC 3339 time or YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive, whole day)
parameters.name: to_date

get.description: One revision with its full snapshot (content, meta, tags, media, SEO) and diff against the previous revision.

post.description: Copies the revision's title, slug, excerpt, content, comment policy, category, cover, tags, and media back onto the post as a new revision of type restore. The post keeps its status and published_at. Categories, tags, and media that no longer exist (or media that is not ready) are skipped and listed in skipped; if another post took the slug, the current slug stays.

get.description: The post's stored SEO overrides (empty fields fall back to derived values), its slug, and advisory warnings such as a title longer than 60 characters. Authors see only their own posts.

put.description: Partial update: omitted fields stay unchanged, "" clears a text field, and null clears an image. Text is trimmed and whitespace-collapsed; markup is rejected. Canonical and og:url hosts must be the site host or in seo.canonical_allowed_hosts. Changing slug needs post.slug.edit. Every invalid field is listed in error.details with a code (too_long, invalid_format, markup_not_allowed, host_not_allowed, not_found, not_image, slug_taken, slug_reserved).

post.description: Renders the search snippet, Open Graph card, and Twitter card the post would get with the submitted SEO fields and optional unsaved title and excerpt. Nothing is saved.
Returns a published or scheduled post to draft and clears published_at.
Names are 2-60 characters of a-z, 0-9 and '_'. Permissions must be registered keys; "*" is reserved for the admin role.

delete.description: Removes the role, its grants, and its user assignments. The admin role cannot be deleted.

put.description: Overwrites the role's permission set; an empty list clears it. The admin role's set is fixed.

get.description: Returns the settings catalogue with current values. server_only keys are never returned; admin_only keys need include_sensitive_admin=true and settings.update.

parameters.description: site, content, media, analytics, notifications, seo, or security
parameters.name: category

put.description: Validates every key, then applies the changed ones atomically. Any invalid key rejects the whole request with 422; a stale per-key version returns 409.

post.description: Creates an active account. Assigning roles also requires role.manage.

get.description: Every audit entry the user performed or that targets the user's account, with IP, user agent, request id, and before/after changes. Requires user.activity.read_all.

post.description: Emails the user a new reset link, invalidating earlier links. Sessions are revoked unless revoke_sessions is false.

delete.description: Administrators cannot revoke the admin role from themselves.
delete.summary: Revoke a role from a user

get.description: The current decisions of the subject identified by X-Consent-Token. An unknown or missing token is 404: treat it as no consent.

post.description: Records a decision per purpose (analytics, authenticated_analytics) with the policy version the visitor saw. Send the X-Consent-Token from an earlier response to update that subject; without it (or with an unknown token) a new subject is created and its token is returned once, with 201. Refusing a granted purpose withdraws it; withdrawing analytics deletes the analytics events already stored for the subject. authenticated_analytics needs a signed-in user and granted analytics, and links the subject to that user.

delete.description: Withdraws one consent. Prove ownership with the subject's X-Consent-Token, or as the signed-in user the subject is linked to; otherwise 404. Withdrawing analytics also withdraws authenticated_analytics, unlinks the user, and deletes the analytics events already stored for the subject. Withdrawing a consent that is not granted changes nothing.

post.description: A move from one page to another. from is omitted for an entry page; transition is internal, external, back_forward, or direct. Accepted asynchronously like page views.

Records a page load. The path's query and fragment are dropped. id (optional, a UUID) is the page view id that time-spent heartbeats refer to; it is generated when omitted and returned either way. Events are written asynchronously: 202 does not mean the event was stored (bots, prefetches, and visitors who refused consent are dropped silently). With analytics.consent_required on, a granted X-Consent-Token is required (403 analytics.consent_required); without granted consent, events are stored without a link to any subject.

A search the visitor ran. The query is lowercased, whitespace-collapsed, and cut to 200 characters. filters may hold category, tag, from, and to. The response id (the client's id when sent) is the search_id to send with result clicks. Accepted asynchronously like page views.

A click on result position (from 1) of search search_id, pointing at a post, page, category, or tag. Neither id is checked against stored data, so the endpoint reveals nothing about what exists. Accepted asynchronously like page views.

A heartbeat for page view view_id with the cumulative seconds the page has been in focus (clamped to 4 hours). Send one every 15-30 seconds while the page is visible and one on unload; the highest value is kept. Accepted asynchronously like page views.
post.summary: Record time spent on a page

post.description:
Exchanges the challenge_token from POST /api/v1/auth/login and a 6-digit TOTP code
or a backup code for a token pair. A challenge expires after 5 minutes or 5 wrong codes.

Returns a token pair, or for accounts with two-factor enabled
`{"two_factor_required": true, "challenge_token", "expires_at", "expires_in"}`
to complete at POST /api/v1/auth/2fa/challenge.

429.description: rate limited or account locked; see Retry-After

503.description: two-factor account but 2FA is not configured

post.description:
Exchanges the code and state the provider sent to the client's redirect_uri. Signs in
the account linked to the provider identity, or the existing account whose email the
provider verified (the identity is then linked). No account is ever created.
Responds like POST /api/v1/auth/login: a token pair or a two-factor challenge.

get.description:
Returns the provider authorization URL (with state and a PKCE challenge) for the
browser to visit. redirect_uri must be listed in OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS. The state
is single use and expires after 10 minutes.

post.description:
Starts a sign-up while the `security.registration_enabled` setting is on and emails a
verification token, valid for 24 hours, to complete at POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email. The answer
is the same `202` whether or not the email already has an account; that account is
emailed about the attempt instead. No account exists, and the username stays free,
until the email is verified. At most 3 unexpired sign-ups per address are kept; further
attempts send nothing. Limited to 10 requests per hour per client IP.

Exchanges the emailed sign-up token, together with the password chosen at sign-up, for an
active account with a verified email, and signs it in (same token pair as login, with a
7-day session). Requiring the password means neither someone who registered another
person's address nor the owner of an address someone else registered can activate the
account alone. A wrong password counts toward the login lockout. Using a token removes
every other pending sign-up for the address.
post.summary: Verify email and activate a registered account

429.description: rate limited or locked; see Retry-After

get.summary: Get a comment with its first replies

delete.description: Soft delete: the comment stays in the thread as a placeholder without content or author.

patch.description: Authors may edit their own comment within the edit window after posting.

post.description: Repeat flags from the same user (or guest IP and user agent) are accepted but counted once.

post.summary: Toggle my upvote on a comment

parameters.description: password and a TOTP or backup code
parameters.name: body

post.description: Replaces every backup code after checking a current TOTP code; the new codes are shown only once.
Enables two-factor with a code from the authenticator and returns 10 backup codes, shown only once.

Returns a new TOTP secret and otpauth:// URL. Calling it again replaces an
unconfirmed secret; it is refused once two-factor is enabled.

get.description: Sign-ins, security changes, and content actions on or by the caller's account, newest first. IP addresses are reduced to their network and user agents to "browser on OS".

post.description:
Queues the anonymization of the caller's account: activity, consents, sessions, and tokens
are deleted; email, name, username, avatar, and profile are scrubbed; posts and comments stay,
shown as "Deleted user". Runs within minutes and cannot be undone. Repeating the call while
the erasure is pending returns the same request.

get.description:
Queues a JSON export of everything stored about the caller, or returns the open or still
downloadable one. 202 while it is being prepared (poll this endpoint); 200 with a short-lived
download_url once ready. After the archive expires, the next call queues a new export.

post.description: Multipart field "file". JPEG, PNG, WebP, or GIF identified by content (not the declared type), at most 8192x8192.

get.description: All of the caller's comments except deleted ones, newest first, including pending and rejected.

post.description: Consumes the token sent to the new address, marks it verified, and revokes every session.
Verifies the password and sends a confirmation token to the new address; the current address gets a notice.

Subscribes the account email to lists (the default lists when empty). A verified account
email joins at once unless double_optin_required is set; otherwise the lists stay pending
until the emailed confirmation link is used (status pending_confirm).

get.description:
The subscription for the signed-in account (linked, or matching the account email) and the
lists that can be chosen. subscribed is false when there is none.

post.description: Leaves lists; empty lists leaves every list and stops all newsletter mail.

get.description: In-app notices (replies, moderation outcomes, publications), newest first. The X-Unread-Count header holds the unread total across all pages.

Server-sent events. The stream opens with `retry: 5000` and `event: stream.opened`, sends `event: notification.created` for each new notice (id is the notification id), `event: ping` when idle, `event: error` with code fanout.buffer_full when events were dropped for a slow client, and `event: stream.closed` before a server shutdown (code shutdown) or once the impersonation session behind the token ends (code impersonation_ended). There is no replay: after reconnecting, call GET /api/v1/me/notifications to fill gaps. Returns 429 notifications.stream_limit (with Retry-After) past the per-user limit and 503 notifications.stream_unavailable without a message broker.

post.description: Idempotent: a notification that is already read keeps its first read_at.

put.description:
Partial update; omitted flags are kept. Narrowing visibility_profile (public → unlisted → private)
requires current_password; widening it and the other flags do not.

patch.description: Allowlisted fields only; omitted keys are kept, null clears, unknown keys are rejected.

get.description: Validates the width against MEDIA_TRANSFORM_WIDTHS and redirects to a signed, expiring imgproxy URL. Images are never enlarged. Without imgproxy configured the endpoint answers 501.

parameters.description: width in pixels, one of MEDIA_TRANSFORM_WIDTHS
parameters.name: w

parameters.description: output format; omitted keeps the source format
parameters.name: format

post.description:
Uses the token from the confirmation email. The pending lists become active and a welcome
email with a preferences link is sent. A token works once.

Sends a new confirmation link to a pending address. Always 202 with the same body, and at
most 3 emails per address in 30 minutes.

get.description:
The subscription behind a preferences token (welcome email and issue footers): masked address,
status, format, list memberships, and the lists that can be chosen.

patch.description:
Changes format and lists by preferences token. lists is the complete set to receive; chosen
lists are active at once, including after an earlier unsubscribe. An empty lists array or
unsubscribe_all stops all mail.

post.description:
Emails a double opt-in confirmation link. Always 202 with the same body whether the address
is new, pending, already subscribed, or suppressed, so it cannot reveal who subscribes. lists
are list slugs (empty means the default lists). Leave honeypot empty. turnstile_response is
required when Turnstile is configured. Rate limited per IP and per address.

Stops all newsletter mail for the subscriber behind an unsubscribe token (email footer).
Also the RFC 8058 one-click target: mail clients POST List-Unsubscribe=One-Click as a form
to this URL with ?token=. The token may be sent in the JSON body or the token query
parameter. Repeating it is harmless.

For the delivery provider. The body is {"events":[{"type":"hard_bounce|soft_bounce|complaint",
"email":"...","occurred_at":"RFC 3339"}]} (1-100 events), signed like outgoing custom_http
requests: X-Newsletter-Timestamp (Unix seconds, within 5 minutes) and X-Newsletter-Signature
v1=hex(HMAC-SHA256(NEWSLETTER_HTTP_SECRET, timestamp + "." + body)). Hard bounces and complaints
suppress the address. 422 when NEWSLETTER_HTTP_SECRET is not set.

get.description:
Newest first. With q, runs a full-text search instead: best match first, and each item
gains search.rank, search.title, and search.snippet (HTML-escaped, matches in <mark>).
q uses web search syntax: "quoted phrase", or, -excluded.
Top-level comments by default; pass parent_id to list the direct replies of a comment.

post.description: Signed-in users comment as themselves. Guests send author_name and author_email when guest comments are enabled; guest comments await moderation. When the server has TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY set, guests must also send turnstile_response.

get.description: Rendered meta for a published post: title, description, canonical URL, robots, Open Graph, and Twitter card values with every fallback applied. Sends X-Robots-Tag when the post is noindex or nofollow.
Looked up by username or user UUID. Private profiles are 404 except for the owner and admins.

author_name.description: Guest commenters only; ignored when a bearer token is sent.

content.description: Plain text or markdown; HTML is not rendered.

honeypot.description: Leave empty. Anti-spam trap for bots; must stay hidden in forms.

turnstile_response.description: Cloudflare Turnstile token; required for guests when the server has TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY set.

notify_author.description: Recorded in the moderation log for author notifications.

preheader.example: Three posts you may have missed

category_id.description: Category UUID; null clears the category, omitting the field keeps it.

comment_policy.description: Who may comment: open, authenticated, read_only, or disabled (hides existing comments).

Bearer.description: Type "Bearer" followed by a space and the JWT access token.
Bearer.name: Authorization
